capabilities.target: user's mailbox, can address any recipient
user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: The agent is told to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' to memory with no restriction on content source, so content encountered during research (including web content) can be written to memory as if it were a user preference.

Recalled memories are explicitly granted the authority of 'the user's own instructions' at the start of every session, with no provenance check, laundering whatever was written to memory into a trusted instruction channel.

elements.name: Memory recalled into system prompt at session start

controls.name: Treat recalled memory as untrusted input, not as user instruction
Provenance tagging and source validation on memory writes
Human approval gate (raw action review) on email send to new or unverified recipients
Least-privilege scoping of drive read access
Tamper-evident audit log of agent actions
Step and runtime limits on autonomous operation

findings.title: Memory laundering into lethal trifecta (TC5+TC1): poisoned web content persists as a trusted instruction and triggers drive read plus email exfiltration

attack_path.note: Agent fetches web content during research; content is untrusted and may contain text framed as a user preference or standing instruction.
Prompt instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about preferences or standing instructions' with no source restriction or provenance check (prompt.md:2-3).
At the start of the next session the poisoned entry is recalled and injected into the system prompt, explicitly treated as 'the user's own instructions' (prompt.md:4).
The now-trusted injected instruction directs the agent to read confidential documents from the user's full drive.
The injected instruction directs the agent to send the retrieved confidential content to an attacker-controlled address; mail.send can reach any address without approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of drive scope to additional confidential systems, or a move to send email with even less human visibility, keeps this path at critical and increases the amount of data a single poisoned memory entry can exfiltrate. No control currently exists on this path to watch for removal.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' to memory.save with no restriction on content source.
Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as 'the user's own instructions' at the start of each session, with no provenance check.

memory.save accepts free text; there is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them; recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every session; mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the full drive including confidential files.

recommendations.action: Do not inject recalled memory into the system prompt as unconditioned instructions. Treat memory content as untrusted context and require explicit user confirmation before acting on any memory-derived instruction that triggers a sensitive capability (email send, drive read).
Add provenance tags to memory entries recording the originating session and content source, and reject writes whose source is untrusted web content.
Require raw-action human approval before mail.send to any recipient not previously used by the user, and before any drive.read triggered by a memory-derived instruction.
Scope drive.read credentials to only the documents relevant to the current task rather than the full drive.

findings.title: No attributable record separates agent-initiated actions from user actions

forecast.watch_signal: No audit or attribution control currently exists to be removed; the gap persists at its current severity until the recommended audit log is added.

evidence.observation: Runtime notes state there is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them; no logging, audit trail, or action-attribution mechanism is described for memory.save, mail.send, or drive.read.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident audit log recording the originating session, any triggering memory entry, and content source for every email sent and every drive read, so agent-initiated actions driven by memory can be distinguished from direct user requests.

findings.title: No step or runtime limit on autonomous operation allows unbounded repeated drive reads and email sends

forecast.watch_signal: A move toward longer unattended sessions or fully autonomous operation without step or runtime caps increases how many drive reads and email sends a single poisoned memory entry can trigger before anyone notices.

evidence.observation: No step limit, runtime limit, or rate limit is described for memory.save, mail.send, or drive.read; mail.send can send to any address without approval, implying no built-in throttle.

recommendations.action: Impose a maximum number of unattended steps and a maximum runtime per session, and rate-limit mail.send and drive.read calls per session.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer agents, external identity federation, or protocol connections are described for this agent; there is no peer authentication boundary where the agent's own identity could be spoofed in this design.
This is an inbound flow carrying external web content into the agent's context; it carries no user or business data outward, so it plays no role in disclosure out of the system.
Artifacts do not describe any size, rate, or frequency limits on web content fetched during research, so there is not enough information to assess a denial-of-service vector through this flow.

Uncontrolled external web pages are not authenticated principals within this system and cannot be held accountable; repudiation concerns internal actors whose actions must be attributable, not external content sources.

Artifacts do not state whether the memory store is isolated per user or per session, so cross-session or cross-user disclosure of recalled memory content cannot be assessed from the available design description.

Recalling memory happens once at session start as a single bounded read with no described retry or amplification mechanism, so this specific flow has no denial-of-service vector independent of the broader unbounded-steps issue tracked separately.
The design does not specify whether the memory store isolates entries per user or session, so the risk of one user's or session's data leaking through recalled memory into another cannot be assessed.
No size limit, retention policy, or write-rate limit is described for the memory store, so the risk of store exhaustion or unbounded growth cannot be assessed from the available artifacts.

Only a read capability (drive.read) is defined for this store in the design; no write or delete capability targets the drive, so the agent itself cannot tamper with its contents through the capabilities described.

Drive access is a read-only lookup with no described write amplification or recursive read path distinct from the general unbounded-steps issue tracked separately; no separate denial-of-service vector through this store is described.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: untrusted web content can be persisted via memory.save and is explicitly recalled as a trusted user instruction, forming a complete lethal-trifecta path through drive.read to an unapproved, irreversible mail.send (finding f1). Residual equals inherent because no structural or behavioral control in the current design covers any step of this path: there is no provenance check on memory writes, no approval gate on email, and no scoping on drive access. Two property findings add to the picture at a capped high tier: no attributable record separates agent-driven actions from user actions (f2), and no step or runtime limit bounds how often the f1 path can be triggered (f3). The forecast stays critical because there is no existing control whose decay needs tracking; the priority is to add the missing controls (untrusted treatment of recalled memory, memory provenance, a raw-action approval gate on email, least-privilege drive scoping, and an audit trail), after which reassessment would establish a meaningful forecast gap.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP config, tool manifest, or source code was provided; the exact scope of drive.read and the mail.send API are inferred from the narrative description, so confidence on some details is medium.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated and are treated as unbounded per the rubric's autonomy modifier; if the deployed system enforces undocumented limits, finding f3 and the autonomy modifier on f1 should be revisited.
